news.headline: India Faces Diplomatic Squeeze Amid US-China Interactions and Pakistan References
news.story_lead: Recent diplomatic developments involving high-level international interactions have raised strategic considerations for India. Media reports highlight shifting dynamics as major global powers engage with regional actors, prompting analysis of India's foreign policy posture.
news.full_article_text: Recent diplomatic reports indicate that India is navigating a complex geopolitical environment. Amid high-profile interactions between global leaders such as Donald Trump, Xi Jinping, and references concerning Pakistan's leadership under Sharif, analysts observe that India faces strategic pressures. These dynamics require careful diplomatic balancing in India's foreign relations, particularly concerning regional security and major power competition.
news.background_context: India's foreign policy relies on strategic autonomy, balancing relationships with major global powers including the United States and managing regional sensitivities involving China and Pakistan.
bullet_points: High-level diplomatic interactions involving global leaders have drawn strategic attention.

news.upsc_analysis: In the context of international relations, India's foreign policy of multi-alignment and strategic autonomy is tested when major powers engage simultaneously with rival regional states. Maintaining independent partnerships without compromising core security interests remains a primary challenge for Indian diplomacy.

Regional diplomatic maneuvers involving India's neighbors.

news.headline: Russia Supports India's UN Security Council Seat Claim, Excludes Germany and Japan
news.story_lead: Russia has expressed firm support for India's claim to a permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council (UNSC). Simultaneously, Moscow has ruled out inclusion for Germany and Japan, citing their alignment with Western positions on global issues.
news.full_article_text: In a significant diplomatic development regarding global governance, Russia has reiterated its backing for India's candidature for a permanent seat in the United Nations Security Council (UNSC). At the same time, Moscow has firmly shut the door on the aspirations of Germany and Japan to join the elite permanent member body. Russia's stance highlights ongoing geopolitical alignments and disagreements regarding the long-overdue reforms of the United Nations Security Council.
news.background_context: The United Nations Security Council consists of five permanent members (P5) with veto power—China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom, and the United States—and ten non-permanent members elected for two-year terms. India has long pushed for UNSC reforms, arguing that the current structure fails to reflect contemporary geopolitical realities. Germany and Japan, along with India and Brazil, form the G4 grouping that mutually supports each other's bids for permanent seats.

Russia rejected the candidatures of Germany and Japan for permanent UNSC membership.
Moscow cited Germany and Japan's alignment with Western policies as a primary reason for exclusion.

Russia opposes permanent membership for Germany and Japan.
exam_relevance: Prelims: International groupings, United Nations bodies
Mains (GS Paper II): Bilateral relations, Global governance, UN reforms and India's position
news.upsc_analysis: India's pursuit of a permanent seat in the UNSC is a key pillar of its foreign policy. Russia's continued backing aligns with the long-standing strategic partnership between New Delhi and Moscow. However, the opposition to Germany and Japan highlights the polarization within the international community regarding the expansion criteria and geopolitical positioning of aspiring nations.

government_steps: Continuous diplomatic engagement at multilateral forums advocating for UNSC restructuring
constitutional_or_policy_link: Guided by India's policy of strategic autonomy and multilateralism
way_forward: Build broader international consensus through sustained diplomatic dialogue
Engage with all P5 members to minimize opposition to India's inclusion
news.mains_notes: Russia's backing of India's permanent UNSC membership highlights bilateral trust, while its rejection of Germany and Japan underscores the fault lines in global governance reforms. India must continue its diplomatic outreach to secure broad-based support.

news.headline: External affairs minister S Jaishankar takes aim at Pakistan at UN, says perpetrator of terrorism must mend its ways
news.story_lead: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar delivered a strong message targeting Pakistan at the United Nations. He stated that it is for the perpetrator of terrorism to mend its ways, emphasizing India's consistent stance on cross-border terrorism.
news.full_article_text: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar took direct aim at Pakistan during his address at the United Nations. Highlighting India's stance on global security and cross-border terrorism, Jaishankar remarked that it is incumbent upon the perpetrator of terrorism to mend its ways. The statement reflects India's ongoing diplomatic efforts at international forums to highlight the issue of terrorism emanating from its neighborhood and to reiterate that normal relations depend on an environment free of terror.
news.background_context: India and Pakistan have a long-standing diplomatic tension primarily rooted in the issue of cross-border terrorism and the status of Jammu and Kashmir. India consistently utilizes international platforms like the United Nations to raise awareness about state-sponsored terrorism and urge global accountability.

news.headline: Man shoots sister and cousin in Haridwar over suspected relationship: Police
news.story_lead: A man in Haridwar's Jhabreda area allegedly shot his sister and a distant cousin on Saturday using a country-made pistol. According to senior police officers, the accused suspected that the two were in a relationship. Police have deployed three teams and initiated surveillance to trace the absconding accused.
news.full_article_text: A tragic incident unfolded in Jhabreda Kalan village within Haridwar's Jhabreda area, where a man identified as Aman Kashyap allegedly shot his distant cousin Suraj alias Munna and his sister Roopa. The event occurred on Saturday, leaving the community in shock. According to police reports, Aman first shot Suraj while he was resting at his home. Following this, the accused went to his own residence and shot his sister Roopa with the same country-made pistol before fleeing the spot. All three individuals—Aman, Roopa, and Suraj—are aged between 20 and 25 years. Local villagers informed the police control room, prompting a swift response from a Jhabreda police station team led by station house officer Praveen Singh and Superintendent of Rural police Abhay Pratap Singh. Haridwar senior superintendent of police Navneet Singh Bhullar stated that the attack stemmed from the accused's suspicion and disturbance over his sister and Suraj being in an alleged relationship. Authorities have collected forensic evidence and deployed three police teams utilizing manual and digital surveillance to trace the absconding accused.
news.background_context: The incident took place in Jhabreda Kalan village in the Jhabreda area of Haridwar, Uttarakhand. Police officials including SSP Navneet Singh Bhullar, SHO Praveen Singh, and Superintendent of Rural police Abhay Pratap Singh are handling the investigation and search operations.

hindi_translation.story_lead: हरिद्वार के झाबरेड़ा क्षेत्र में शनिवार को एक व्यक्ति ने कथित तौर पर अपनी बहन और दूर के चचेरे भाई को एक देशी पिस्तौल से गोली मार दी। वरिष्ठ पुलिस अधिकारियों के अनुसार, आरोपी को संदेह था कि दोनों के बीच रिश्ता था। पुलिस फरार आरोपी की तलाश के लिए तीन टीमों को तैनात कर निगरानी कर रही है।

news.headline: Election Commission Extends Delhi SIR Deadline and Waives Mandatory ERO Hearings Amid Internal Review
news.story_lead: The Election Commission of India has announced key modifications to the ongoing Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, including waiving mandatory personal hearings before Electoral Registration Officers and extending deadlines for Delhi and Maharashtra. The decisions come amidst internal discussions regarding IT systems and oversight.
news.full_article_text: The Election Commission of India (ECI), chaired by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, announced significant procedural changes concerning the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Under the revised guidelines, voters who receive notices during the SIR process for being unmapped or having logical discrepancies are no longer required to make personal appearances before the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO). Instead, Booth Level Officers (BLOs) will conduct home visits to collect necessary documents, which will be subsequently uploaded to the ECINet portal for final ERO decision. Personal hearings will now be restricted to exceptional circumstances, preferably conducted online. Furthermore, district election officers have been directed to establish adequate help desks and special camps for vulnerable populations, including night shelter residents, labourers, the poor, and the homeless. The Commission also announced that a committee headed by a senior deputy election commissioner, along with an independent expert from an IIT or IIIT, will review the ECINet system to ensure compliance with relevant acts and rules. Additionally, reacting to requests from chief electoral officers, the ECI extended deadlines for filing claims and objections and their disposal in Delhi and Maharashtra.
news.background_context: The decisions follow internal discussions and reports regarding work allocation and control of the poll panel's IT systems, as well as prior guidelines and Supreme Court upholdings concerning the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.
bullet_points: Voters issued notices during the SIR for being unmapped or having discrepancies no longer need mandatory personal ERO hearings.
BLOs will collect documents through home visits and upload them to the ECINet portal.
A committee including an independent IIT/IIIT expert will review the ECINet portal for compliance.
Deadlines for claims, objections, and their disposal were extended for both Delhi and Maharashtra.
District election officers were ordered to set up help desks and special camps for the homeless, labourers, and the poor.
key_facts: Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar chaired the ECI meeting.
Delhi SIR claims and objections deadline extended till October 30, 2026, with disposal till November 30, 2026.
Maharashtra SIR filing deadline extended till October 12, 2026, with disposal till November 10, 2026.

Mains: Governance, electoral reforms, administrative transparency, institutional functioning of constitutional bodies.
news.upsc_analysis: The functioning and internal transparency of the Election Commission of India form a crucial component of Indian polity and governance. Procedural amendments in electoral roll revisions directly impact voter disenfranchisement risks, administrative efficiency, and the protection of democratic rights for marginalized sections. Reviews of digital infrastructure like ECINet underscore the increasing intersection of technology and electoral management in India.

news.headline: EAM S Jaishankar Leads Indian Delegation at 81st UNGA Session in New York
news.story_lead: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar is leading the Indian delegation at the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York. On the sidelines of the UNGA High-Level Week, he has engaged in multiple bilateral meetings with counterparts from Russia, Iran, and the United States, while also launching a new shipping safety grouping with Liberia.
news.full_article_text: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar is in New York leading the Indian delegation at the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA). Scheduled to address the High-Level Session of the UNGA during the morning session of the General Debate, EAM Jaishankar is slated to speak towards the end of the session. During the High-Level Week, Jaishankar has held diplomatic discussions with several key counterparts, including Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Discussions ranged from bilateral issues and BRICS cooperation to regional conflicts in the Gulf and Ukraine. Furthermore, India and Liberia jointly launched the 'Group of Friends on Safety and Security of Shipping and Seafarers' to address recent attacks on commercial vessels on the high seas, which have resulted in seafarer casualties, including an Indian sailor.
news.background_context: The United Nations General Assembly High-Level Week involves world leaders gathering in New York to discuss pressing global issues, bilateral relations, and multilateral cooperation. India continues to engage actively in international forums like BRICS and the UN while addressing maritime security concerns on global shipping routes.
bullet_points: EAM S Jaishankar is leading India's delegation at the 81st Session of the UNGA in New York.
He held bilateral and multilateral discussions with counterparts from Russia, Iran, and the US.
India and Liberia launched the 'Group of Friends on Safety and Security of Shipping and Seafarers' on the UNGA sidelines.
Discussions with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio included India's concerns regarding the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act (SRIA).
Jaishankar highlighted growing concerns over commercial shipping attacks in the Gulf, Red Sea, and Black Sea.

news.headline: Uttarakhand Woman and Lover Arrested for Mother's Murder Over Property Dispute
news.story_lead: Police in Uttarakhand have arrested a 36-year-old woman and her lover for allegedly murdering her 65-year-old mother in Raiwala over an ancestral property dispute. The arrests followed a thorough police investigation involving CCTV footage analysis and technical surveillance.
news.full_article_text: Uttarakhand Police have arrested 36-year-old Shilpa Thapa and her partner, 39-year-old Shiv Narayan Pandey alias Sonu, for the murder of 65-year-old Khajani Devi. The deceased lived in a rented house in Shaheed Bhagat Singh Colony in Motichur's Linepar with her six-year-old granddaughter. The case came to light when the victim's son, Sanjay Pundir, lodged a complaint at the Raiwala police station stating that his mother had been missing and the house was locked, later discovering her body inside the bathroom. Following directions from Dehradun Senior Superintendent of Police Pramendra Dobhal, six teams were formed to investigate the crime using forensic evidence, CCTV footage from roughly 700 cameras, and informant networks. According to police, Shilpa conspired with Pandey because she believed her mother and brother were selling ancestral land without giving her a share. She falsely told Pandey that Khajani was her stepmother. Pandey, who was under financial pressure after suffering business losses and debt, allegedly strangled the victim on September 21 while she was alone and subsequently hid in Haridwar before being arrested.
news.background_context: The incident occurred in Raiwala, Uttarakhand, originating from a familial dispute over ancestral land and financial pressures faced by the accused.
bullet_points: A 36-year-old woman and her lover were arrested for murdering her 65-year-old mother in Raiwala, Uttarakhand.
The murder stemmed from a dispute over ancestral property and land distribution.
Police formed six teams, examined footage from about 700 CCTV cameras, and searched around 500 hotels and guesthouses.
The co-accused, facing financial losses and debt, allegedly strangled the victim while she was alone at home.
Both suspects have been taken into custody following police investigation and technical surveillance.

Accused: Shilpa Thapa (daughter) and Shiv Narayan Pandey (partner/lover).

Date of incident: September 21.
Arrest locations: Shantikunj in Haridwar and Shaheed Bhagat Singh Colony.

From an administrative and law enforcement perspective, it demonstrates the utility of technical surveillance, CCTV analysis, and coordinated police action in solving complex crimes.

hindi_translation.story_lead: उत्तराखंड पुलिस ने रायवाला में पैतृक संपत्ति के विवाद को लेकर अपनी 65 वर्षीय मां की हत्या करने के आरोप में 36 वर्षीय महिला और उसके प्रेमी को गिरफ्तार किया है।

news.headline: Supreme Court Dismisses BJP MLAs' Plea Against Karnataka Energy Minister KJ George in Smart Meter Tender Case
news.story_lead: The Supreme Court has dismissed an appeal filed by three BJP legislators challenging the Karnataka High Court's decision to quash a case against Karnataka Energy Minister KJ George. The case involved allegations of irregularities in a ₹4,985-crore smart electricity meter tender awarded by BESCOM. A bench of justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran found no merit in the appeal and upheld the high court's ruling.
news.full_article_text: The Supreme Court on Friday dismissed a special leave petition filed by three Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) legislators — CN Ashwathnarayan, SR Vishwanath, and Dheeraj Muniraj — seeking the prosecution of Karnataka Energy Minister KJ George. The legislators alleged irregularities in the allocation of a ₹4,985-crore smart electricity meter tender. The apex court upheld the Karnataka High Court's December 2025 order, which had earlier quashed the case after finding no merit in the allegations. The bench, comprising justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran, stated that it found no good ground to interfere with the high court's order. The allegations pertained to 2024, when the petitioners claimed that the energy minister, serving as the chairman of Bangalore Electricity Supply Company Limited (BESCOM), colluded with officials to manipulate financial thresholds and award the tender to M/s Rajashree Electricals Pvt Ltd. The high court had previously observed that the allegations did not disclose criminality and that the tender process was transparent with participation from multiple bidders and no allegations of bribery.
news.background_context: The case stems from a 2024 complaint by three BJP MLAs regarding a ₹4,985-crore smart electricity meter tender awarded by BESCOM to M/s Rajashree Electricals Pvt Ltd. The complainants initially approached the Lokayukta, which declined to direct an investigation, before filing a case before a Bengaluru trial court. In July 2025, the trial court sought a report from the Lokayukta, prompting KJ George and other accused to approach the Karnataka High Court, which quashed the case in December 2025. The Supreme Court has now dismissed the appeal against the high court's decision.
bullet_points: The Supreme Court dismissed an appeal by three BJP MLAs seeking prosecution of Karnataka Energy Minister KJ George.
The case involved allegations of irregularities in a ₹4,985-crore smart electricity meter tender.
The apex court upheld the Karnataka High Court order from December 2025 that had quashed the case.
The bench consisted of justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran.
The Karnataka High Court had earlier ruled that the allegations did not disclose criminality and pointed to a transparent tender process.
The tender was awarded by Bangalore Electricity Supply Company Limited (BESCOM) to M/s Rajashree Electricals Pvt Ltd.

Energy Minister of Karnataka: KJ George
Petitioners: CN Ashwathnarayan, SR Vishwanath, and Dheeraj Muniraj

UPSC Mains GS Paper II: Statutory, regulatory and various quasi-judicial bodies; Accountability and transparency in public procurement
news.upsc_analysis: This case highlights the intersection of public procurement, judicial review, and political accountability in India. It underscores the scope of high courts and the Supreme Court in examining criminal complaints arising from administrative and tender processes, ensuring that standard commercial disputes or transparent administrative decisions are not unnecessarily criminalized without prima facie evidence of criminality or quid pro quo.

The judiciary emphasized the absence of criminality and noted the transparency of the bidding process, reinforcing that administrative decisions without evidence of bribery or quid pro quo should not be prematurely criminalized.

news.headline: Indian Diplomat's Viral Reaction at UNGA Follows Clash Over Operation Sindoor and Cross-Border Terrorism
news.story_lead: A video of Indian diplomat R Srinivas reacting with a smirk to Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's claims at the United Nations General Assembly has gone viral. The diplomatic exchange highlighted ongoing tensions following the May 2025 military confrontation between India and Pakistan.
news.full_article_text: A viral video from the United Nations General Assembly captured Indian diplomat R Srinivas appearing to smirk and shake his head as Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif claimed victory during last year's military confrontation. Sharif addressed the UNGA, detailing Islamabad's account of the four-day conflict in May 2025, which followed India's Operation Sindoor launched after the Pahalgam terror attack. Sharif also credited US President Donald Trump for preventing further escalation, a claim countered by India's assertion that the ceasefire was achieved through direct bilateral communication. Exercising India's right of reply, First Secretary Petal Gahlot strongly criticized Pakistan, accusing the country of cross-border terrorism, deceit, and duplicity, while warning that terrorism will have consequences.
news.background_context: The diplomatic sparring at the UN General Assembly follows a four-day military confrontation between India and Pakistan in May 2025, designated as Operation Sindoor, which was initiated by India following the Pahalgam terror attack.
bullet_points: Indian diplomat R Srinivas was captured on camera smirking during Pakistani PM Shehbaz Sharif's UNGA speech.
Sharif claimed victory regarding the May 2025 military confrontation known as Operation Sindoor.
Operation Sindoor was launched by India following the Pahalgam terror attack.
Sharif credited US President Donald Trump for preventing further escalation, which India refuted by stating the ceasefire was agreed bilaterally.
First Secretary Petal Gahlot exercised India's right of reply, slamming Pakistan for cross-border terrorism and duplicity.
key_facts: The military confrontation between India and Pakistan occurred in May 2025.

exam_relevance: UPSC Mains Paper II - International Relations, Bilateral Relations involving India and its neighbours, and multilateral forums like the UN.
news.upsc_analysis: The diplomatic exchanges at international forums such as the UNGA highlight India's consistent policy of holding neighbouring states accountable for cross-border terrorism while firmly rejecting third-party mediation claims in bilateral disputes. India's official stance emphasizes bilateral mechanisms for ceasefires and unyielding opposition to state-sponsored terrorism.

impacts: Amplification of bilateral tensions on multilateral platforms like the UNGA.

challenges: Persistent cross-border terrorism and conflicting narratives from neighbouring states at international forums.
government_steps: India exercised its right of reply at the UNGA through First Secretary Petal Gahlot to strongly reject false claims and emphasize accountability for cross-border terrorism.
constitutional_or_policy_link: Article 51 of the United Nations Charter concerning self-defence, referenced during the UN addresses.
way_forward: Continued diplomatic resolve in isolating state sponsors of terror on global stages while maintaining strategic clarity on bilateral dispute resolution.
news.mains_notes: India's robust diplomatic response at the UNGA underscores its zero-tolerance approach towards cross-border terrorism and its rejection of third-party mediation in bilateral matters with Pakistan.

news.headline: 2 Naga civilians killed by unknown armed individuals in Manipur's Senapati district
news.story_lead: Two Naga civilians were killed by unknown armed individuals at Kailenjang village in Manipur's Senapati district. This incident occurred just a day after four Tangkhul Naga civilians were killed at Pilong village in the Kamjong district.
news.full_article_text: Two Naga civilians were killed by unknown armed individuals at Kailenjang village in Manipur's Senapati district on Saturday. The deceased have been identified as Rocky from Mao Chaowainamai village and Kumar from Poumai Laii Shirafii. This incident took place just a day after four Tangkhul Naga civilians were killed at Pilong village in the border district of Kamjong, allegedly by armed individuals across the Indo-Myanmar border. The recent violence follows developments involving the United Naga Council (UNC), a Naga apex body, which announced the suspension of its indefinite economic blockade on all national highways in Manipur following tripartite talks held in Guwahati.
news.background_context: The United Naga Council (UNC) had imposed an indefinite inter-district economic blockade on all national highways in Manipur starting May 17. The agitation was launched after the state government failed to fulfill ultimatums to locate six Nagas who were allegedly abducted on May 13 by a group of Kuki individuals at Leilon Vaiphel village following ambushes in Noney and Kangpokpi districts. Following the recovery of the six Naga civilians as mutilated bodies, the UNC intensified its demands, including the abrogation of the Suspension of Operation (SoO) agreement with Kuki militants, the arrest of perpetrators, and the removal of Deputy Chief Minister Nemcha Kipgen. The economic blockade was subsequently suspended following tripartite talks among the Government of Manipur, the Government of India, and the UNC in Guwahati on September 26, 2026.
bullet_points: Two Naga civilians were killed by unknown armed individuals at Kailenjang village in Manipur's Senapati district.
The deceased were identified as Rocky from Mao Chaowainamai village and Kumar from Poumai Laii Shirafii.

Mains (GS Paper 2/3): Internal security challenges in Northeast India, ethnic conflicts, tribal rights, and conflict resolution mechanisms.

Incidents involving different ethnic groups, such as Nagas and Kukis, along with the intervention of apex bodies like the United Naga Council, require nuanced administrative and political conflict-resolution strategies by both state and central governments.

news.headline: Bengaluru Man Arrested for Wife's Murder After Body Found in Vacant Plot
news.story_lead: A 32-year-old man from Odisha was arrested more than three weeks after allegedly killing his wife in Bengaluru following a financial dispute. The accused kept the body at home for three days before dumping it in a vacant plot.
news.full_article_text: A 32-year-old man, Sagar Chandra Rawat from Odisha, was arrested by Bengaluru police for allegedly murdering his 26-year-old wife, Anusuya, following an argument over finances on August 11. According to police, the accused assaulted and strangled his wife, resulting in her death due to suffocation. Sagar kept the body inside their Bengaluru home for about three days before wrapping it in a bedsheet, tying it with a rope, and dumping it at a vacant plot in MS Nagar near Sampigehalli around midnight. The highly decomposed body was discovered on September 2 by civic workers who were cleaning the plot following a directive by the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) for property owners to maintain their premises. Due to the decomposed state of the body, police faced difficulties in identifying the victim until a mall tag on her clothing, a Ganesha pendant, and subsequent technical analysis helped trace her identity and address. Police subsequently took Sagar into custody, where he confessed during interrogation after being confronted with discrepancies in his statement.
news.background_context: The incident occurred in Bengaluru, Karnataka, highlighting urban crime detection methods, police investigations utilizing mall tags and technical analysis, and municipal sanitation directives issued by the Greater Bengaluru Authority.

news.headline: ECI Clarifies Procedure for 'Unmapped' and 'Logical Discrepancies' Notices During Special Intensive Revision
news.story_lead: The Election Commission of India (ECI) has announced that electors receiving notices for being 'unmapped' or having 'logical discrepancies' during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) will generally not need to appear personally before the Electoral Registration Officer. Instead, Booth Level Officers will visit homes to collect necessary documents for upload on the ECINet portal.
news.full_article_text: Following a meeting of the full Commission at Nirvachan Sadan, the Election Commission of India (ECI) issued guidelines regarding notices sent during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Electors flagged with 'unmapped' details or 'logical discrepancies' are generally exempt from personal appearance before the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) or Assistant Electoral Registration Officer (AERO). Booth Level Officers (BLOs) will visit the homes of such electors to collect required documents, which will then be uploaded to the ECINet portal for ERO decision-making. Personal hearings are restricted to exceptional circumstances determined by the ERO and, where necessary, will preferably be conducted online with strengthened facilities. Additionally, electors can authorise any adult family member to attend the hearing on their behalf. The ECI also directed district election officers to set up adequate help desks and special camps for night shelter residents, labourers, the poor, and the homeless. Furthermore, a committee headed by a senior deputy election commissioner, including an independent expert from an IIT or IIIT, will review the ECINet system to ensure compliance with relevant Acts and Rules.
news.background_context: The guidelines were announced following a full Commission meeting at Nirvachan Sadan, attended by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, amid ongoing revisions and extensions of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

news.headline: Nirma University Orders Probe After Professor Grabs Student's Collar on Stage
news.story_lead: Nirma University in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, has ordered a seven-day inquiry into a confrontation between a professor and a student during a campus event. A viral video showed the professor grabbing the student's collar after a remark was made during a performance by comedian Rajat Sood. The incident triggered protests by student bodies like ABVP and NSUI, leading to university intervention.
news.full_article_text: A private university in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, Nirma University, has initiated a seven-day inquiry following a confrontation between a faculty member and a student during a campus event. The incident occurred during Technofora 2026, a student event organized by the university's Institute of Technology held from September 18 to 20. The confrontation took place after a performance by comedian Rajat Sood. According to the viral video circulating on social media, Professor H K Patel, head of the Electrical and Instrumentation Engineering department, was addressing the audience when a student shouted a dialogue from the 2010 film Golmaal 3 ('Jaldi kar, Panvel nikalna hai'). In response, Professor Patel called the student to the stage, grabbed his collar, and questioned his conduct, warning that he could 'go to any extent' if a faculty member was insulted. Following the viral video, student wings including the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) and the Congress-affiliated National Students’ Union of India (NSUI) staged protests. NSUI sought an impartial inquiry, CCTV preservation, and protection for the student. Meanwhile, university director general R N Patel stated that a three-member committee of senior deans and directors has been formed to examine the incident and submit a report within seven days. Both the professor and the student have reportedly apologized to each other, and the student's parents have been contacted.

news.headline: Election Commission Clarifies Nature of Letters Sent to Cabinet Secretary Amid Internal Discussions
news.story_lead: The Election Commission of India has clarified that letters sent by election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi to Cabinet Secretary T V Somanathan were regarding the functioning of an officer on deputation, rather than any policy matter or IT division policy. The clarification follows internal discussions and media reports regarding work allocation and oversight of the ECINet platform.
news.full_article_text: The Election Commission of India (ECI) addressed a key meeting following reports of differences between election commissioners and Chief Election Commission Gyanesh Kumar regarding work allocation and technology platforms. In a press note, the ECI stated that letters sent by election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi to Cabinet Secretary T V Somanathan were concerning the functioning of an officer on deputation, rather than policy matters or the commission's IT division. The commission noted that work redistribution orders issued by the concerned officer were not implemented after directives from the two commissioners, and oversight of the IT division by the Deputy Election Commissioner was never withdrawn. Reports had previously highlighted concerns raised by the commissioners regarding ECINet, a unified technology platform launched on January 22 to streamline applications and portals. Commissioners had flagged issues concerning access control and the centralisation of the electoral roll database, proposing an outside IIT expert audit to ensure compliance with statutory provisions. In response, the ECI announced that a committee headed by a Senior Deputy Election Commissioner, including an independent expert from an IIT or IIIT, will review ECINet to ensure compliance with Acts and Rules. Furthermore, the ECI maintained that ECINet is a decentralised platform where statutory functions remain strictly with designated field officers using individual credentials.
news.background_context: The Election Commission of India launched ECINet on January 22 as a unified technology platform combining over 40 applications and portals. Internal discussions and media reports highlighted differing views among commissioners regarding work allocation and access control for state-level election officials updating electoral rolls.

news.headline: Heavy Rains and Thunderstorms Claim Six Lives, Damage Over 100 Houses Across Uttar Pradesh
news.story_lead: Heavy rains, thunderstorms, and strong winds driven by a depression over Madhya Pradesh have lashed Uttar Pradesh, resulting in six deaths and damage to over 100 houses. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued warnings for heavy to very heavy rainfall, potential flash floods, and gusty winds across multiple districts.
news.full_article_text: Uttar Pradesh has experienced intense downpours with 63 districts recording above-normal rainfall, driven by a weather system comprising a depression over northeast Madhya Pradesh and adjoining north Chhattisgarh. The system moved north-northwestwards towards southeast Uttar Pradesh. The extreme weather resulted in six rain-related fatalities, five of which occurred due to mud-wall collapses in Lakhimpur Kheri, Amethi, and Barabanki, and one due to a roadside tree falling on a motorist in Barabanki. Over 117 houses have been damaged, and standing crops in rural areas have suffered losses due to heavy winds and waterlogging. The IMD has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall at several places in eastern Uttar Pradesh and central Terai regions, alongside squally winds reaching 40-60 kmph. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has directed district administrations to remain vigilant, inspect vulnerable areas, and ensure school closures in districts under red alerts or flash flood risks. Special vigilance has also been ordered in districts bordering Nepal due to rising river levels.
news.background_context: The severe weather event is triggered by a depression centered over northeast Madhya Pradesh and adjoining north Chhattisgarh, which moved towards southeast Uttar Pradesh, bringing widespread heavy to very heavy rainfall and gusty winds.

news.headline: Election Commission extends electoral roll deadlines in Maharashtra and Delhi amid revision updates
news.story_lead: The Election Commission has extended the deadlines for filing claims and objections related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls to October 12 in Maharashtra and October 30 in Delhi. The decision follows reports of internal differences among the three-member commission regarding electoral roll revisions and work allocation. The poll body also announced that voters receiving notices for unmapped and logical discrepancies will be visited at home by Booth Level Officers rather than appearing for mandatory personal hearings.
news.full_article_text: The Election Commission of India has announced extensions for filing claims and objections related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. In Maharashtra, the deadline has been extended to October 12, with the disposal deadline moved to November 10. Similarly, in Delhi, the claims and objections deadline is extended to October 30, and disposal to November 30. This announcement comes in the wake of reports concerning differences among the three-member Election Commission over decisions related to electoral roll revisions, including the addition and deletion of names, changes to forms, and access to voter data. Commissioners SS Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had previously written to Cabinet Secretary TV Somanathan objecting to changes in work allocation that allegedly removed oversight over the IT backbone of electoral rolls. In response to the revision process, the Commission clarified at a meeting that its June 24, 2025 SIR order was issued with unanimous approval and upheld by the Supreme Court. Furthermore, voters receiving notices during the SIR for being unmapped or having logical discrepancies are no longer required to personally appear before the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO). Instead, Booth Level Officers (BLOs) will visit them at home to collect required documents, which will be uploaded to the ECINet portal. District election officers have also been directed to establish help desks and special camps for vulnerable groups such as labourers, the homeless, and residents of night shelters.
news.background_context: The Election Commission undertook a Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, which has already been completed in 20 states and Union Territories, including Bihar and West Bengal. Internal reports highlighted differences among election commissioners regarding work allocation and IT oversight, prompting the poll body to reiterate that its revision schedules and orders had unanimous approval and Supreme Court backing.

news.headline: Odisha rain: Over 73,000 affected, 40,000 evacuated as rivers rise
news.story_lead: Heavy rainfall triggered by a deep depression has severely impacted Odisha, affecting over 73,000 people across 10 districts. Authorities have evacuated more than 40,000 individuals to safer locations as water levels in several rivers rise.
news.full_article_text: Heavy rain triggered by a deep depression has affected more than 73,000 people across 10 districts of Odisha, with over 40,000 people evacuated to safer locations, officials said on Saturday. The affected areas include 80 blocks, 325 gram panchayats, 1,071 villages and 49 wards in 10 urban local bodies, according to the latest government assessment. Sixteen villages have remained waterlogged, while 721 houses were partially or fully damaged and 4,480 hectares of cropland were affected. Mayurbhanj was among the worst-affected districts, with 20,475 people affected in 144 villages across 20 blocks. There has been no report of human or livestock casualties so far. Meanwhile, rising water levels in several rivers have raised fears of flooding in parts of the state. The Subarnarekha river was rising following heavy rain in its upper catchment, raising fears of flooding in the Basta, Baliapal, Bhograi and Jaleswar areas. Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari said southern Odisha had been particularly affected, with Koraput, Nabarangpur, Malkangiri, Rayagada, Ganjam and Gajapati districts witnessing widespread impact. Pujari noted that heavy rain in the upper catchments of Chhattisgarh has increased water flow in the Mahanadi, while rainfall in Jharkhand is expected to affect parts of northern Odisha.
news.background_context: Odisha is frequently impacted by heavy rains, deep depressions, and cyclonic storms originating in the Bay of Bengal, which often lead to swelling rivers, agricultural losses, and displacement of populations across southern and northern districts.

news.headline: TDP Chief N Chandrababu Naidu Welcomes Election Commission's Unanimous Clarification Amid Voter Rolls Row
news.story_lead: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu has hailed the unanimous clarification issued by the Election Commission of India (ECI) regarding decisions made by the poll panel. The statement followed an investigative media report alleging dissent among election commissioners, prompting calls for transparency from various political parties.
news.full_article_text: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister and TDP chief N Chandrababu Naidu welcomed the unanimous clarification issued by the Election Commission of India (EC), stating that it reaffirmed the integrity and credibility of constitutional institutions. The clarification was issued jointly by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar alongside election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, putting to rest misconceptions surrounding the poll panel. The EC reasserted that key decisions, including the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls, were taken unanimously by the full commission. This clarification came in the wake of an investigative report by The Indian Express, which claimed that election commissioners had recorded objections to decisions taken in the commission's name multiple times over a ten-month period. The report triggered protests and demands for resignation from opposition parties like the Congress, as well as calls for clarification from NDA constituents such as the Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) and Rashtriya Lok Morcha. TDP leaders emphasized that maintaining transparency and addressing questions helps strengthen public confidence in constitutional institutions.

This led to opposition protests and calls from BJP allies for transparency regarding the poll panel's internal functioning.

news.headline: Gauhati University student found dead at homestay in Assam; male friend arrested
news.story_lead: A 22-year-old student of Gauhati University was found unconscious at a homestay near Azara on the outskirts of Guwahati, Assam, and was later declared brought dead at a hospital. Police have arrested a male friend, identified as Ashik Ali, in connection with the incident as an investigation is underway.
news.full_article_text: A 22-year-old Gauhati University student, Nimisha Thakuria, was found unconscious at a homestay near Azara on the outskirts of Guwahati, Assam, and subsequently declared brought dead at Guwahati Medical College & Hospital (GMCH). According to police reports, she had gone out with a friend and stayed at the homestay. Bolin Deori, DCP (West), stated that three youths brought her to Azara Primary Health Centre in the early hours of Saturday before she was referred to GMCH. Police arrested Ashik Ali in connection with the incident, and he remains in police custody. news.headline: TMC Chief Mamata Banerjee and Abhishek Banerjee to Attend INDIA Bloc Meeting on September 30
news.story_lead: Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee and TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee are scheduled to attend the INDIA bloc meeting on September 30. The meeting aims to discuss the Election Commission and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), bringing political rivals CPI(M) and TMC together in a rare show of political solidarity.
news.full_article_text: Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee and TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee will attend the upcoming INDIA bloc meeting on September 30. The meeting is set to deliberate on issues concerning the Election Commission and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). This development brings together political rivals CPI(M) and TMC in a rare display of solidarity. AITC chief Mamata Banerjee previously held talks with CPI(M) general secretary MA Baby and Congress MP Rahul Gandhi to coordinate the meeting. Addressing a rally in Hooghly, Banerjee raised concerns regarding the SIR process, alleging that it was forced upon West Bengal to capture the state politically, and claimed that millions of names were struck off electoral rolls. In contrast, the Election Commission has stated that the revision exercise is aimed at ensuring the integrity and accuracy of electoral rolls, maintaining that differences within institutional processes are part of normal deliberations. The INDIA bloc, originally formed in 2023 ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, has experienced internal differences over electoral strategies and state-level political equations, but Banerjee's latest appeal highlights a unified effort to address common institutional issues.
news.background_context: The INDIA bloc was formed in 2023 ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, bringing together parties with different ideological positions and competing regional interests. Its initial meetings were held in Patna in June 2023 and Bengaluru in July 2023. In West Bengal, the TMC, Congress, and CPI(M)-led Left Front contested the 2024 Lok Sabha elections separately.

news.headline: Child drug abuse is a child protection issue, not just health: CJI Surya Kant
news.story_lead: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant stated that child drug abuse must be addressed as a child protection issue alongside public health. Emphasizing dignity, confidentiality, and rehabilitation, the CJI warned that social stigma and lack of institutional sensitivity can silence victims and discourage them from seeking help.
news.full_article_text: Addressing a seminar in Patna on 'Restoring Childhood, Preventing Drug Abuse and Re-integration of Children in Need of Care and Protection,' Chief Justice of India Surya Kant highlighted that child substance abuse requires a sensitive, multi-stakeholder approach focused on dignity and confidentiality. He noted that more than one in five teenagers in India are at moderate-to-high risk of substance use, citing an August 2026 study published in The Lancet Regional Health – Southeast Asia. The CJI stressed that children struggling with substance use should not face humiliation or carry permanent labels, and that the legal and justice systems must distinguish firmly between drug traffickers and child victims requiring safety, treatment, counseling, and rehabilitation. He further underlined that a coordinated effort involving the judiciary, government, police, health and education systems, child-care institutions, and civil society is essential for the successful social re-integration of affected children.
news.background_context: The Supreme Court of India has been actively dealing with the rising concern of substance abuse among children. According to an August 2026 study in The Lancet Regional Health – Southeast Asia, more than one in five teenagers in India face moderate-to-high risk of substance use. The CJI addressed these concerns during a seminar in Patna and later participated in an open-house dialogue at Chanakya National Law University (CNLU).
bullet_points: CJI Surya Kant emphasized that child drug abuse is both a public health concern and a critical child-protection issue.
Confidentiality and dignity are vital for effective rehabilitation, preventing victims from remaining silent due to social stigma.
Cited an August 2026 study from The Lancet Regional Health – Southeast Asia showing over one in five Indian teenagers are at moderate-to-high risk of substance use.
Called for a clear distinction between the legal response to drug traffickers/perpetrators and child victims needing treatment and care.
Stressed a multi-stakeholder framework involving police, hospitals, schools, families, courts, and civil society for holistic re-integration.

For civil services aspirants, this highlights the intersection of juvenile justice, public health policy, and the need for multi-sectoral institutional convergence to protect vulnerable demographics.

news.headline: 17-year-old Nikita Kumari shines as India beat Iran to win kabaddi gold
news.story_lead: Haryana's 17-year-old Nikita Kumari delivered a crucial performance on her senior India debut, helping the women's kabaddi team defeat Iran to win the gold medal at an international tournament. Brought onto the mat during a difficult situation, the teenager showcased exceptional mental toughness and an attacking performance under pressure.
news.full_article_text: Haryana's 17-year-old Nikita Kumari made a memorable senior debut for India, delivering a crucial performance in the final as the women's kabaddi team defeated Iran to win gold at an international tournament on Saturday. For Nikita, who is among the youngest members of the Indian squad representing the country at the international level, kabaddi has been a part of her surroundings since childhood. She started playing the sport at the age of eight. Her coach, Sunil Dabas, noted that her upbringing in the villages of Haryana and early entry into sports helped her build the mental toughness required for the international stage. Before joining the senior team, Nikita had established herself at the junior level, representing India in youth competitions and captaining the Indian junior side. During the final against Iran—widely considered one of the strongest teams in Asian women's kabaddi—India found itself in a difficult situation. Brought onto the mat at a crucial juncture, Nikita responded with an attacking performance that gave India the necessary impetus. Despite facing intense physical pressure and a rough style of play from Iran, and suffering an injury, she continued playing to secure victory. Back home in her village, her family, including her mother Vinod Kumari and three younger sisters who also play kabaddi, celebrated her achievement by distributing sweets to neighbours.
news.background_context: The match featured India against Iran, a team noted by coaches to be among the strongest in Asian women's kabaddi, with matches between the two sides often becoming intensely physical. news.headline: Cockroach Janta Party and Congress Demand CEC Gyanesh Kumar's Resignation Following Allegations
news.story_lead: Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar is facing calls for resignation from the Cockroach Janta Party and Congress MP Rahul Gandhi following allegations by a former Kerala bureaucrat that Kumar offered him a BJP candidature in 2016. Meanwhile, the Election Commission has defended its decision-making process as unanimous and legally sound.
news.full_article_text: Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar is at the center of a political controversy after former Kerala chief secretary Jiji Thomson alleged that Kumar had asked him if he was interested in contesting the 2019 Lok Sabha elections as a BJP candidate while travelling on a flight together in 2016. Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Abhijeet Dipke renewed calls for Kumar's resignation, stating 'Gyanu must go' and announcing plans for a nationwide protest campaign starting October 2 in Mumbai. The CJP's 'Election Commission Thik Karo' campaign focuses on the exclusion of over 13 crore names from draft electoral rolls across 30 states and Union Territories during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise. Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray has also backed the protest call. Congress MP Rahul Gandhi criticized Kumar on X, accusing him of 'match-fixing elections'. In response to the controversy and reports of alleged differences between election commissioners, the Election Commission reasserted that key decisions, including the SIR of voter rolls, were taken unanimously by the full commission with full legal sanction.
news.background_context: The controversy follows an investigative report by The Indian Express alleging differences between the election commissioners and CEC Gyanesh Kumar. The Election Commission maintains that differing views are normal during institutional deliberations and that orders follow statutory procedures.

Allegations against high-ranking election officials raise questions regarding the independence of election management bodies, which are foundational to India's democratic framework. news.headline: Tamil Nadu YouTuber’s Social Media Wealth Flaunting Backfires as Burglars Steal Gold Jewellery
news.story_lead: A YouTube content creator in Tamil Nadu faced a major burglary after posting videos flaunting her family's wealth, cash, and gold jewellery. Police suspect the perpetrators monitored her online activity before breaking into her home in Nagercoil and stealing approximately 118 sovereigns of gold.
news.full_article_text: In recent times, the intersection of social media exposure and personal security has emerged as a significant societal concern. A Tamil Nadu-based content creator named Madhumitha, who runs a YouTube channel sharing lifestyle videos and reels, became the victim of a major heist after posting content showcasing her family's affluent lifestyle. In one viral video, she was seen showering her child with stacks of ₹500 notes and mentioning that she purchases gold jewellery every month. After returning from a short trip to Tirunelveli, Madhumitha and her family discovered that approximately 118 sovereigns of gold jewellery kept in a bureau had been stolen. Police in Nagercoil have launched an exhaustive investigation, deploying fingerprint experts, forensic teams, and analyzing CCTV footage alongside social media trail data to trace the culprits. The incident highlights the growing risks associated with oversharing personal details and high-value assets on public digital platforms.
news.background_context: The incident occurred in Nagercoil, Tamil Nadu, following a short family trip to Tirunelveli. In southern India, gold is commonly measured in units called 'savaran', 'pavan', or 'sovereign'. The content creator frequently posted lifestyle reels and videos detailing her family's financial affluence and regular gold purchases.

news.headline: Uttarakhand bans high-frequency sound systems near Badrinath Dham and Chamoli religious sites
news.story_lead: The Chamoli district administration in Uttarakhand has banned events using high-frequency sound systems near the Badrinath Dham temple and other religious sites with immediate effect. The decision comes in response to objections raised by citizens, religious leaders, and devotees against a recent cultural festival held near the shrine.
news.full_article_text: The Chamoli district administration in Uttarakhand has implemented an immediate ban on events near the Badrinath Dham temple and other religious sites that compromise their sanctity through high-frequency sound systems. District Magistrate Gaurav Kumar has mandated that prior permission from the local administration is compulsory for organizing any event near religious and cultural sites in the district, including Shri Badrinath Dham. Only the concerned Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) is authorized to examine and issue permissions for such proposed events. The directive follows objections from religious leaders, devotees, and civil society members regarding the two-day Devbhoomi Cultural Festival 2026, held on September 19 and 20 at the tourist arrival plaza near Badrinath Dham. While critics argued that high-intensity sound systems affect the spiritual environment of the major Hindu pilgrimage center, organizers and state authorities maintained that the festival was a civil-military integration and socio-economic initiative under Operation Sadbhavana, jointly organized by the district administration and the Army to strengthen ties with border residents and armed forces personnel.
news.background_context: The order was issued by Chamoli district administration following public and religious objections to the Devbhoomi Cultural Festival 2026 held on September 19 and 20 at the tourist arrival plaza near Badrinath Dham, which was organized jointly by the district administration and the Army under Operation Sadbhavana.
bullet_points: Chamoli district administration banned high-frequency sound systems near Badrinath Dham and other religious sites with immediate effect.

news.headline: Jaishankar Slams Pakistan PM at UNGA Over Terrorism and Misrepresentation of Facts
news.story_lead: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar has strongly criticized Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif at the United Nations General Assembly for misrepresenting facts and attempting to normalize terrorism. India also exercised its Right of Reply, calling Pakistan a puppet regime and asserting its right to self-defence against cross-border terrorism.
news.full_article_text: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar addressed the United Nations General Assembly, slamming Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif for misrepresenting facts and invoking arguments to normalize terrorism and claim immunity from its consequences. Without naming Sharif directly, Jaishankar asserted India's right to self-defence and stated that friendship and goodwill cannot coexist with terrorism. Pakistan's Prime Minister had earlier spoken about a four-day military confrontation between India and Pakistan in May 2025, claiming Islamabad exercised self-defence under Article 51 of the UN Charter and crediting US President Donald Trump for timely intervention. New Delhi rejected these claims, maintaining that the ceasefire was reached through direct bilateral communication. Following the address, India exercised its Right of Reply, with First Secretary Petal Gahlot describing Pakistan as a puppet regime and criticizing its record on cross-border terrorism, democratic rights, and minority treatment.
news.background_context: Following the Pahalgam terror attack in April 2025 which caused the deaths of 26 civilians, India launched Operation Sindoor on May 7, striking terror bases in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir. The military escalation concluded with a ceasefire on May 10, 2025.

Jaishankar accused Pakistan of being a 'serial practitioner of terrorism' seeking immunity from consequences.
India asserted its right to self-defence and stated that friendship cannot coexist with terrorism.

New Delhi firmly maintained that the May 2025 ceasefire was reached via direct bilateral communication without third-party intervention.
India exercised its Right of Reply through Petal Gahlot, calling Pakistan a 'puppet regime' and highlighting its cross-border terrorism.

news.headline: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar Invokes PM Modi's UNGA Remarks on Global Conflicts
news.story_lead: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar addressed the United Nations General Assembly, highlighting how countries far from ongoing conflicts are being penalized. Invoking Prime Minister Narendra Modi's previous remarks, Jaishankar emphasized the adverse global impacts of ongoing wars on energy security, maritime trade, and supply chains.
news.full_article_text: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar called upon the United Nations General Assembly to face up to the true state of affairs regarding global conflicts. Voicing serious concerns over countries across the world suffering due to ongoing wars, Jaishankar stated that nations far from conflicts are being penalized for no fault of their own and that those most impacted often have the least say. He invoked Prime Minister Narendra Modi's earlier remarks made at the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, where PM Modi highlighted that the crisis in West Asia impacts the entire world's energy security, maritime trade, and supply chains, heavily affecting the Global South. Jaishankar specifically pointed to the unrest in West Asia and the Gulf, expressing deep concern over continuing hostilities and the unacceptable attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers transiting international waterways such as the Strait of Hormuz. India called upon all parties to exercise restraint, de-escalate tensions, protect civilians, and ensure the uninterrupted flow of energy and commerce. Addressing the conflict in Ukraine, now in its fifth year, Jaishankar reiterated PM Modi's stance that endless war must give way to peace, supporting ongoing diplomatic initiatives. Furthermore, he highlighted India's readiness to assist in mitigating global food and energy security challenges, noting that a durable and lasting peace in the Middle East requires a two-state solution.
news.background_context: The statements were delivered by External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar during the United Nations General Assembly, referencing earlier geopolitical assessments made by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at multilateral forums like the SCO regarding ongoing global conflicts such as the Ukraine war and the West Asian crisis.

hindi_translation.story_lead: विदेश मंत्री एस जयशंकर ने संयुक्त राष्ट्र महासभा को संबोधित करते हुए कहा कि संघर्षों से दूर स्थित देशों को भी दंडित होना पड़ रहा है। प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी की पिछली टिप्पणियों का हवाला देते हुए जयशंकर ने वैश्विक युद्धों के ऊर्जा सुरक्षा, समुद्री व्यापार और आपूर्ति श्रृंखला पर पड़ने वाले प्रतिकूल प्रभावों पर जोर दिया।
hindi_translation.full_article_text: विदेश मंत्री एस जयशंकर ने संयुक्त राष्ट्र महासभा से वास्तविक स्थिति का सामना करने का आह्वान किया। दुनिया भर में चल रहे युद्धों के कारण देशों के पीड़ित होने पर चिंता व्यक्त करते हुए जयशंकर ने कहा कि संघर्षों से दूर स्थित देशों को बिना किसी गलती के दंडित किया जा रहा है और सबसे अधिक प्रभावित होने वालों की सबसे कम सुनी जाती है। उन्होंने किर्गिस्तान के बिश्केक में शंघाई सहयोग संगठन (एससीओ) के राष्ट्राध्यक्षों की परिषद की बैठक में प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी द्वारा दिए गए पहले के बयानों का हवाला दिया। जयशंकर ने पश्चिम एशिया में अशांति पर प्रकाश डालते हुए कहा कि इस वर्ष हम खाड़ी में संघर्ष देख रहे हैं। उन्होंने अंतरराष्ट्रीय जलमार्गों और होर्मुज जलडमरूमध्य में वाणिज्यिक जहाजों पर हमलों को अस्वीकार्य बताया। भारत ने सभी पक्षों से संयम बरतने, तनाव कम करने और ऊर्जा एवं वाणिज्य के निर्बाध प्रवाह को सुनिश्चित करने का आह्वान किया।
hindi_translation.background_context: ये बयान विदेश मंत्री एस जयशंकर द्वारा संयुक्त राष्ट्र महासभा में दिए गए, जिसमें यूक्रेन युद्ध और पश्चिम एशियाई संकट जैसे वैश्विक संघर्षों पर पीएम मोदी के पिछले भू-राजनीतिक आकलन का संदर्भ दिया गया।
bullet_points: विदेश मंत्री एस जयशंकर ने संयुक्त राष्ट्र महासभा को संबोधित किया।
बताया कि संघर्षों से दूर देशों को बिना किसी गलती के दंडित किया जा रहा है।
पीएम मोदी के एससीओ बयान का हवाला दिया कि कैसे पश्चिम एशियाई संकट वैश्विक ऊर्जा और व्यापार को प्रभावित करता है।
होर्मुज जलडमरूमध्य में वाणिज्यिक जहाजों पर हमलों की निंदा की।
मध्य पूर्व के लिए द्वि-राज्य समाधान का समर्थन किया।
key_facts: एस जयशंकर ने संयुक्त राष्ट्र महासभा को संबोधित किया।
पीएम मोदी ने पहले बिश्केक, किर्गिस्तान में एससीओ बैठक में पश्चिम एशिया संकट पर बात की थी।
